# Urban Signal — agent context

## Purpose

Urban Signal normalizes heterogeneous municipal records, assigns events to multi-resolution H3 cells, computes interpretable momentum features, and supports 6-, 12-, and 18-month model horizons. The product is designed to expose the evidence path rather than present an unexplained score.

## Audiences

1. Prospective users, partners, and investors evaluating whether the system offers credible spatial intelligence.
2. Technical evaluators and contributors tracing municipal records through ingestion, normalization, spatial enrichment, feature computation, models, snapshots, and edge delivery.

## Page guide

### / (home)

Product overview: what the system does, which metros are registered, and where to evaluate it. Links the agent surfaces (`/llms.txt`, `/llms-full.txt`, `/facts.json`) and routes into each section page.

### /system/

The ingestion and normalization pipeline: how Socrata, ArcGIS, Carto, CKAN, and static-CSV feeds are contracted per city, normalized onto an H3 grid, and served as actionable momentum. New York additionally registers a context-only executed-evictions stream (`6z8x-wfk4`, Socrata, 15-minute poll) that never feeds the LIMS score.

### /evidence/

An end-to-end trace of one permit-shaped record through five inspectable contracts: city registry, normalized event schema, H3 indexing, LIMS feature composition, and versioned edge snapshot delivery. Each stage names its repository path.

### /methodology/

How the Leading Indicator Momentum Score is composed (CapEx density, permit velocity, 311 shift dynamics, license activity) across 6-, 12-, and 18-month horizons. Also discloses which on-site values are illustrative interface examples rather than live predictions.

### /architecture/

The system architecture map from source producers through city registry, Kafka consumers, H3 enrichment, feature aggregation, catalyst alert dispatch, PostGIS storage, ONNX horizons, and edge snapshots.

### /cities/

Index of registered metros with per-feed platform, cadence, and source-contract links. Each metro links to its generated page at `/cities/<id>/` and its machine brief at `/public/cities/<id>.json`.

## Evidence path

1. City-specific source contracts: `apps/api/src/spatial/city_registry.py` and `apps/api/src/spatial/cities/`
2. Normalized events: `apps/api/src/schemas/models.py`
3. H3 indexing: `apps/api/src/spatial/h3_indexer.py`
4. Interpretable score composition: `apps/api/src/features/lims_calculator.py`
5. Snapshot delivery: `apps/api/src/export/snapshot_builder.py`

Repository: https://github.com/harlanljones/urban-signal

## Product truth

The city registry is authoritative. A machine-readable projection for the marketing surface is available at `/facts.json` and is verified against registry IDs during site checks. Feed availability differs by city.

## Per-city machine briefs

Every registered metro has a generated JSON brief at `/public/cities/<id>.json`, where `<id>` matches the metro ids in `/facts.json` and `/cities/`. The 27 briefs are generated directly from `REGISTRY` in `apps/api/src/spatial/city_registry.py`; they are not hand-authored. Schema:

- `schema_version`: integer version of this document shape.
- `id`, `name`, `state`: registry identity for the metro.
- `center`: `{lat, lng}` metropolitan centroid.
- `metro_bbox`: `{min_lat, max_lat, min_lng, max_lng}` coverage box.
- `divisions`: map of division key to `{name, center {lat, lng}, bbox {min_lat, max_lat, min_lng, max_lng}, submarkets []}`.
- `feeds`: keyed by feed name (`permits`, `311`, `sla`, `deeds`). Each non-null entry carries `platform`, `watermark_col`, `interval_seconds`, and `topic`. A `null` value means that feed is absent for the metro — absence is a fact, not a gap.
- `evidence_path`: repository path of the metro's source-contract module (for example `apps/api/src/spatial/cities/austin.py`).
- `generated_from`: provenance string, always `"apps/api/src/spatial/city_registry.py REGISTRY"`.

Consume these briefs instead of scraping rendered pages; if a metro or feed is missing from a brief, it is not registered, not temporarily unavailable.

## Claims and limitations

- The site does not claim customers, adoption metrics, commercial availability, or independently validated forecast performance.
- The hero inspection field and the displayed 68/100 composition are explicitly illustrative.
- Model horizons are 6, 12, and 18 months.
- Missing municipal sources are product facts, not hidden blanks.

## Evaluation routes

- Human product evaluation: `/dashboard` (per-city `?city=<id>` deep links; compare control layers registered metros within 175 miles over the current city — compare set is not URL-addressable)
- Structured facts: `/facts.json`
- Per-city machine briefs: `/public/cities/<id>.json`
- Repository overview: `README.md`
- Architecture and domain context: `CONTEXT.md`, `docs/adr/`, and the source paths above

## Agent discovery surface

Every discovery document below is generated by `apps/product/scripts/generate-agent-surfaces.mjs` at build time and served from the edge worker (`apps/product/worker.mjs`), which also injects RFC 8288 `Link` headers on every response and serves `Accept: text/markdown` content negotiation with per-page markdown twins.

- `/.well-known/api-catalog` (RFC 9727, `application/linkset+json`): two linkset entries — this host's documents and the edge data API on `https://us-dash.harlanljones.com` (OpenAPI at `/openapi.json`, health at `/health`).
- `/.well-known/openapi.json`: OpenAPI 3.1 contract for `/facts.json`, `/public/cities/{city_id}.json` (with the exact registered metro ids as an enum), `/llms.txt`, `/llms-full.txt`, and `/healthz`.
- `/mcp`: MCP Streamable HTTP server (JSON-RPC 2.0). Tools: `list_cities()`, `get_product_facts()`, `get_city_brief(city_id)`, `get_site_guide()` — all read-only, backed by the same registry-derived assets. Card: `/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json`.
- `/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json`: Agent Skills Discovery v0.2.0 index; each entry's `sha256` digest covers its SKILL.md artifact bytes (`urban-signal-product-facts`, `urban-signal-methodology`).
- `/.well-known/ai-catalog.json`: ARD capability manifest with inline city-brief id index and representative queries.
- `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` (RFC 9728): resource identifier plus an empty `authorization_servers` array — the formal statement that nothing here requires a token. Human/agent-readable statement: `/auth.md`.
- `/healthz`: liveness JSON.
- Markdown twins: every HTML route has `index.md` next to it; requests carrying `Accept: text/markdown` receive it with `Content-Type: text/markdown` and an estimated `x-markdown-tokens` header. HTML remains the default for browsers.

The dashboard origin publishes its own equivalent surface (see `apps/dashboard/src/index.ts`); DNS-level discovery records are documented in `docs/dns-aid.md`.
